Research reliability · complete paper route

Standalone 180-minute core, calculator and paper/local document. No code or JavaScript required. Keep every attempt, both trial cases, your dated plan, hand work and revision. Optional Python +35 minutes outside core. Assessments are self-reviewed; grades and study times have not been externally validated. No credential is awarded.

Prepare an audit · 15 minutes

Chapter 09 · Self-paced learning

Audit the claim.

A plausible chart is the beginning of a research question. It does not establish that a rule will work. Learn to trace information, retain failed trials and commit to a bounded evaluation before interpreting its result.

Your 180-minute route

Setup 15 · bias audit 30 · trial log 35 · plan 40 · evaluation 35 · revision 25 minutes. Timings are design estimates awaiting learner testing. Use a calculator; no programming required. Optional Python adds 35 minutes.

OBJ-M09 / CLO-05: identify all six planted integrity defects, keep every trial, freeze a reproducible plan and revise a claim using chronological net results. Positive profit earns no marks.

Prerequisites: percentages, compound wealth and Chapter 8's next-open rule. Standalone bridge: a closing signal decides a position only for the next open. A 10bps cost is .001 times traded wealth; £1,000 entry costs £1. Cash earns zero.

This chapter stores only this browser's record. Export before clearing it. Browser timestamps and public source code do not prove preregistration or secure blindness.

Confirm you can use percentages and open/download the supplied CSV; if needed practise 10bps×£1,000=£1. Store your own paper record; it does not synchronise with the interactive route.

Repair the claim · 30 minutes

Which information existed?

Worked audit: “Our close-based rule earned the return ending at that same close.” A signal computed after the close cannot earn an already completed return. Repair: compute the signal using closes through day t, enter at open t+1 and earn the open t+1→t+2 return. Retain both the original flawed claim and correction in the log; do not relabel the old result valid.

Guided audit: twenty windows were tried and only the best reported; the universe omits funds that closed; costs are zero for the strategy but included for the benchmark; dates differ. Report every trial, seek a point-in-time universe, use matched net conventions and limit the conclusion until defects are resolved.

Independent transfer below changes the trial case to six seeds. Attempt first, check, then explain one repair. Every critical answer is required. This is formative practice with a visible key, not a secure exam.

  1. A signal uses Tuesday close and earns Monday-open to Tuesday-open return. Enter 1 retain; 2 repair to next eligible open.
  2. A report shows only the best of 20 tested windows. Enter number of trials the log must retain.
  3. Only currently surviving funds appear in an old-universe test. Enter 1 disclose survivorship and recover point-in-time universe; 2 call the result representative.
  4. Strategy evaluated February; benchmark evaluated January. Enter 1 compare; 2 align the same entry and exit dates.
  5. £1,000 buys once at 10 basis points per notional. Entry cost (£)?
  6. New case: a researcher tries six seeds, reports only a winning seed and calls it an untouched holdout. How many trials must the log retain?
Check after attempting, then revise one repair

future: 2. Tuesday close was unknown at both opens. Use the Chapter 8 next-open timeline.

selection: 20. Retain all 20, including zero or negative results. A holdout does not undo repeated peeking.

survivors: 1. Closed funds cannot simply disappear. Until recovered, limit the claim.

dates: 2. A relative result requires matching investable periods.

cost: 1. 10 / 10,000 × £1,000 = £1. Also charge the exit and benchmark consistently.

transfer: 6. All six; relabel this period as inspected. A new untouched dataset would be needed for a new confirmatory claim.

Every critical item must be correct. Write a specific repair explaining its reason (60+ characters); retain first and corrected attempts.

Retain every trial · 35 minutes

A negative trial is still evidence.

Trial logs prevent quiet selection. A trial is a distinct run or inspected configuration, including errors, failed ideas and unchanged reruns. Record the rule, dates, costs, prediction, result, decision and whether evaluation had already been inspected.

The fixed development demonstration below uses Chapter 8 data only. The two cost levels were specified in advance, not selected to maximise profit. Log both. The evaluation segment later is original synthetic data, result summaries are gated in the interactive evaluation step until your plan is frozen. Data and prepared text-route results remain inspectable in downloads, guides and source files; reading them first is prior exposure that you must disclose.

Worked log row: “3-close / 10bps / development / executed next open / retain even if loss / educational synthetic only.” New task: compare the 30bps case, explain why deleting an unfavourable row would bias interpretation, and name the limit of one market period.

Reproduce these development trials using Chapter 8 rule/text route. 10bps final £956.229145; 30bps final £944.800245. Keep both regardless of sign. Write a 50+ character selection/period limitation.

Freeze your plan · 40 minutes

Decide what will count.

Write a question and a prediction before reveal. The prefilled rule is fixed: close above trailing three-close mean (including current close), long next open or cash; no shorting, leverage or parameter search. Start with £1,000. Benchmark buy-and-hold shares the same eligible opens, initial capital and entry/exit costs. Cash earns 0; taxes, additional slippage, liquidity constraints and dividends are excluded.

Base cost 10bps per traded notional; one sensitivity 30bps. Retain both and all reruns. The deterministic synthetic evaluation segment is Feb 1–16 2026, a later teaching block than Chapter 8. Warmup uses only its first three closes; no position before the first eligible open. Do not combine block returns as continuous live performance.

Freeze an immutable snapshot. If you edit the question or prediction later, current results become stale; freeze a new version. Older plans and runs remain. Once inspected, revised plans are labelled exploratory. The local gate teaches discipline; it does not prove an untouched statistical holdout, a timestamp audit or prevent source inspection.

  1. Write your testable question (30+ characters) and prediction (20+).
  2. Copy the fixed rule, initial wealth, costs, same-date benchmark, synthetic dataset ID, sensitivity and stopping rule.
  3. Record date/version and every prior inspection. Freeze this paper snapshot before opening the next section; preserve it when revising.

Prior inspection cannot be prevented in this document. This plan is pedagogical, not a registry preregistration or proof of blindness. If you read outputs first, label the work retrospective/exploratory.

Reveal and compare · 35 minutes

Reveal, reproduce, qualify.

Before reveal, predict whether the rule will beat its same-period benchmark after costs. Reveal computes both predefined cost cases using the Chapter 8 pure backtest. Re-run unchanged inputs to reproduce; every run is retained, not just the best.

Hand method: first eligible signal uses the first three closes. If invested, end wealth = start wealth × (1 − turnover × costBps/10,000) × (exit open / entry open). If cash, the market factor is 1. A final liquidation cost is charged after the last period. The table lists the inputs needed for the first row; calculate before entering its end wealth.

Do not mistake a synthetic held-out block for independent real evidence. One period, simplified trading, deterministic prices and prior development choices all limit interpretation. An unfavourable result or a decision to reject the strategy can be a successful analysis.

Retain each rerun or manual recalculation, even if unchanged. Match first/last eligible opens and account for benchmark final exit. Write the date/cost/timing/trial integrity checklist.

Revise the conclusion · 25 minutes

Repair the headline.

Original flawed claim: “This always wins because we chose the strongest trial.” Replace it with a bounded conclusion naming both net cost cases, same-period benchmark, chronology and at least three material limits. A sound conclusion can reject the rule or find insufficient evidence.

Self-review criteria: every critical audit item corrected; no hidden trials; plan precedes ordinary-UI reveal or prior exposure disclosed; matching dates/costs; current row hand check; conditional interpretation. Write a concrete revision after inspecting your evidence. Prose is self-reviewed, not automatically validated by length.

Write conclusion (80+ characters) and a specific feedback-linked revision (50+). Self-review all critical audit items, full trial log, frozen-plan caveat, matched net evidence, hand check and three limits. Retain every version. No mark is awarded for a positive return.
